messages.content: The office signed off on the Front Range loop as fly-and-rent, and the Denver fair is now Wednesday evening. Can we turn it into the booking stack for Aug 18-22? I want the Sunday afternoon SLC-DEN, rental from DEN, Boulder or Louisville for Sunday/Monday, then south Denver Tuesday/Wednesday. Please make sure the hotel rooms are queen rooms, not vague bedding, and call out the Boulder cancellation date and parking.

Yes. I’ll build it around two hotel bases and keep the downtown Denver hotel off the table unless it solves more than it costs. Before I pin the flight: is a Thursday return after the Union Station coffee okay, and how much material are you carrying?
After lunch Thursday is fine. I’ll have one checked box of brochures, a rolling carry-on, and the banner. If Delta is close, great, but I do not want to stretch the day for it.

Flight choices that fit: Delta nonstop SLC-DEN Sun 2:40-4:10 and DEN-SLC Thu 2:20-3:55; United nonstop Sun 3:15-4:45 and Thu 1:35-3:10; Southwest nonstop Sun 1:55-3:25 and Thu 4:05-5:40. I’d take the Delta pair if the fare is within policy; the Thursday return gives enough room after coffee without wasting the afternoon.
Use the Delta pair. Window if there is one. I would rather not do the 1:35 return and watch traffic the whole morning.

Good. For the car, I’d reserve a pay-later intermediate SUV at DEN, pickup Sunday about 4:45, return Thursday about 12:30. That gives cargo room without paying for a full-size SUV. Does pay-later work for reimbursement?
Yes, pay-later. Nothing huge unless they substitute it. I need to fit the box out of sight if possible.

Hotel shortlist: Boulder base is Boulder Garden Inn, queen non-smoking, breakfast 6:30-9:30, parking $12/night, cancel by Thu Aug 15 at 6 pm, about $219. Louisville/Superior Suites has a queen studio, breakfast 6:00-9:00, free parking, cancel by Sat Aug 17, about $189, but it is 15-20 minutes farther from the Tuesday breakfast. South Denver: Hampton Greenwood Village, queen, breakfast 6:30-9:30, parking $8/night, cancel by Tue Aug 20, restaurants next door. Residence Inn DTC is roomier but parking is $15.
Take the Boulder Garden Inn even with the Aug 15 cancellation, as long as it is not prepaid. For south Denver, Hampton sounds easier after the fair.

That works. I’d book Boulder Garden Inn for Sun/Mon, cancellable but not prepaid, queen non-smoking; parking budget $24. Hampton Greenwood Village for Tue/Wed, queen non-smoking; parking budget $16. Both list breakfast early enough for the school-day departures, but I’d screenshot the hours with the reservations.
Can you give me the Sunday-through-Thursday driving timeline and the dinner plan? Keep dinners low-effort.

Timeline: Sunday land 4:10, car by 4:45, drive to Boulder, check in around 5:45; dinner near the hotel or Pearl Street, no reservation needed. Monday keep the Boulder base for the Fort Collins visit and any north-side stops; casual dinner in Boulder. Tuesday breakfast in Boulder, then leave for south Denver late morning, check into Hampton before the afternoon prep block; dinner near the hotel. Wednesday leave by 10:30 for Colorado Springs, visit early afternoon, drive back toward downtown Denver for fair load-in, then return to Greenwood Village after the fair. Thursday leave hotel about 7:00 for the Union Station coffee, return car at DEN around 12:30, fly 2:20.
Great. Add package acceptance and the receipt buckets for my admin note.

Final note to send: Book Delta SLC-DEN Sun Aug 18 2:40-4:10 and DEN-SLC Thu Aug 22 2:20-3:55, window seat requested. Reserve pay-later intermediate SUV at DEN, pickup Sun 4:45, return Thu 12:30. Hotels: Boulder Garden Inn Sun/Mon, queen non-smoking, breakfast 6:30-9:30, parking $12/night, cancel by Aug 15 at 6 pm; Hampton Greenwood Village Tue/Wed, queen non-smoking, breakfast 6:30-9:30, parking $8/night, cancel by Aug 20. Ship the brochure box to the Boulder hotel with arrival by Friday and call to confirm they will hold it. Budget downtown fair garage at about $25-35. Receipt categories: airfare, checked box or bag fee if charged, rental car, hotel folios, fuel, hotel parking, downtown fair parking, and airport parking only if used.

memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Tessa kept the Greenwood Village hotel despite the earlier Thursday coffee, chose driving and paid garages over rideshare for material control, decided to check out before the coffee, and made a simple post-fair dinner plan near the hotel while keeping valuables out of sight.

messages.content: The Denver fair load-in email finally arrived and it is annoying. For Wednesday they want us at the 14th Street dock at 4:15, no unattended carts, and the garage they recommend is not connected. Also the Union Station coffee moved to 8:00 Thursday. Is the Greenwood Village hotel still the right call?
It can still work, but it changes the margin. What time does the fair end, and can you leave Colorado Springs by 2:30 after the school visit?
Fair is 5:30 to 7:30. I should be able to leave Colorado Springs by 2:30 unless the counselor runs long. Hotel checkout is noon and breakfast starts at 6:30.

Keep the hotel. Wednesday: leave Colorado Springs by 2:35, aim for the downtown garage by 4:00, and use the paid garage over street parking so you are not circling with boxes. Take the laptop and purse into the fair; leave only sealed brochure boxes under the cargo cover or a blanket.
For Thursday morning, would you drive downtown or rideshare from the hotel?

Drive. With luggage and leftover materials, rideshare adds handoff risk and may not save time. Leave Greenwood Village at 6:45, park in a Union Station-area garage by 7:40, and walk in with only the coffee folder and laptop.
Should I check out before the coffee, then?
Yes. Check out before you leave, ask the desk for a grab-and-go item if breakfast is not fully set, and load the car under the hotel canopy. Do not rearrange bags once you are downtown.
Dinner after the fair: I do not want to wander downtown with the banner.

Then make dinner a hotel-area plan. After the fair, load out, go straight back to Greenwood Village, and eat at one of the restaurants next to the Hampton or place a mobile order before leaving the garage. Budget parking as: hotel $16 total, downtown fair garage about $25-35, Union Station garage about $12-20. The only real timing risk is Colorado Springs running late; if you are not on I-25 by 2:45, call the fair contact and ask whether load-in can be held at the registration table.

messages.content: Colorado is wrapped up and I’m starting the mid-September Pacific Northwest loop. Draft schedule is Sep 15-19: Monday 7:30 counselor breakfast in Vancouver, WA, Monday evening Portland fair, Tuesday school visits around Salem, Wednesday 1:00-4:00 transfer fair in Eugene, and Thursday 10:30 counselor coffee near Corvallis. I need a route comparison before I ask for approval: fly-and-rent, open-jaw, or drive the whole thing from Salt Lake.

I can rank those. A few details will affect whether the open-jaw is worth it: how much material are you taking, are you okay flying out Sunday afternoon, do you need to be home Thursday night, and will the office allow a one-way rental if the fee is reasonable?

Two boxes of brochures plus the pop-up banner. I can ship one box to the first hotel, but not the banner. Sunday afternoon is fine. I’d like to be home Thursday night. A one-way rental is okay if it is not ridiculous.

First pass: 1) Fly SLC-PDX Sunday, rent, return from EUG Thursday: least backtracking, best if the EUG return has one comfortable connection; watch the one-way car fee and smaller-airport disruption risk. 2) Fly SLC-PDX round trip, rent and return at PDX: simplest flights and rental, likely cheaper, but adds the Corvallis-to-PDX drive Thursday after coffee. 3) Drive SLC-Vancouver-Salem-Eugene-Corvallis-SLC: maximum material control and no flight risk, but two very long travel days and probably more fatigue than savings. My practical primary would be to price 1 and 2 side by side; keep 3 as backup only if shipping or fares fail.
I’m not excited about a tiny Eugene connection. If the return from Eugene has one short layover that is 70 minutes or more, fine. If it is a 40-minute scramble, I would rather drive back to Portland.

Good boundary. Approval version: open-jaw wins only if the Eugene return has one connection with about 70-75 minutes or better and gets you to SLC Thursday evening. If the connection is tighter, choose the Portland round trip even though it adds the drive. The full-drive plan should not be the requested plan unless the material load grows.
Sketch the actual Sunday-to-Thursday routing for the two flight versions.

Open-jaw route: Sunday fly SLC-PDX, pick up car, sleep Vancouver or north Portland. Monday breakfast in Vancouver, Portland fair, then drive to Salem for the night. Tuesday Salem visits, then drive to Eugene. Wednesday Eugene fair, then sleep Corvallis if the Thursday coffee is there and the Eugene flight is late enough; otherwise stay Eugene. Thursday Corvallis coffee, drive to EUG, drop car, fly home. Portland round trip: same through Wednesday, but after the Thursday coffee drive Corvallis-PDX, return the car there, and fly home late afternoon or evening.
Where would you put the hotels? I am fine switching, but I do not want to end up with a pretty hotel that makes the first visit harder.

Hotel areas I’d use: Sunday Vancouver waterfront, downtown Vancouver, or Jantzen Beach/north Portland so Monday breakfast is easy and Portland fair access is still reasonable. Monday Salem or Keizer near I-5, because Tuesday starts there. Tuesday Eugene near the university, Valley River, or north Eugene, depending on the transfer fair site. Wednesday Corvallis if the Thursday coffee is definitely near Corvallis; Eugene only if the flight home forces it.
Is it dumb to drive to Salem after an 8:00 pm Portland fair?

Not dumb, but plan it deliberately. Eat before leaving Portland or stop in Wilsonville/Woodburn, then check into a Salem/Keizer hotel with late desk coverage. It buys you a calmer Tuesday morning. Staying in Vancouver Monday night would make Tuesday too dependent on early traffic.
Breakfast and parking need to be in the approval note. The school visits start early enough that I do not want breakfast to be a mystery.

Add hotel criteria rather than specific brands for now: breakfast confirmed by 6:30 in Vancouver/north Portland and Salem, and by 7:00 in Eugene/Corvallis; parking either included or a stated nightly amount; interior storage or front-desk hold for shipped materials. If a hotel cannot confirm breakfast hours, assume a coffee-and-bagel receipt instead of relying on it.
Dinner access too, especially Monday after Portland and Wednesday after Eugene.

Monday dinner: pre-fair early dinner in Portland, or a quick stop on I-5 before Salem. Choose a Salem hotel near restaurants, not an isolated highway exit. Wednesday: if staying Corvallis, pick downtown or riverfront-adjacent so you can get food after the Eugene fair without another drive. If staying Eugene, Valley River or campus-area hotels usually make dinner simpler.
How should I handle materials?

Ship one brochure box to the first hotel for arrival by Saturday and have the label include your name, university, arrival date, and hold for guest. Carry the banner and one core packet set. Each morning, take only that day’s materials; keep extras covered in the cargo area, and never leave the laptop or badge bag in the car.
Can you turn this into a sign-off note with the three options and the recommendation?

Draft sign-off note: For Sep 15-19 Pacific Northwest recruitment loop, request pricing for two flight plans. Preferred if reliable: fly SLC-PDX Sunday afternoon, rent a car, complete Vancouver-Portland-Salem-Eugene-Corvallis route, return from EUG Thursday after the 10:30 Corvallis coffee, only if the return has no more than one comfortable layover and the one-way rental fee is reasonable. Fallback: fly SLC-PDX round trip, same rental from PDX, drive back to PDX after Thursday coffee, and fly home late Thursday. Backup only: full drive from Salt Lake City with materials, used if shipping or fares make flying impractical. Hotel plan: Sunday Vancouver/north Portland, Monday Salem/Keizer, Tuesday Eugene, Wednesday Corvallis unless flight timing favors Eugene. Approval needs to include hotel breakfast hours, parking costs, late dinner access, material hold or shipping fees, fuel, and one-way rental fee if applicable.
One focused revision: if the Eugene return prices well but has a 43-minute layover in Seattle, should I still list it?

No. List that as priced but not recommended. The approval ask should say: choose EUG return only with a connection around 70-75 minutes or longer; otherwise approve the PDX round trip despite the extra drive. For arrival reliability, a cheap 43-minute connection out of Eugene is not worth building the loop around.
